Pick the most distinguishable colours from one or more palettes

Source: R/pick.R
tf_pick.Rd

Pools the colours of the named palettes and selects the n that are hardest to confuse with one another on a given kind of plot: light background, dark background, or output that will be read in greyscale. Optionally judges distinctness under simulated colour-vision deficiency. Use it when a single character's palette does not have enough usable colours, or when you want a team's or a faction's colours but only the ones that hold up on a chart.

Usage

tf_pick(
  palettes,
  n = 5,
  style = c("light", "dark", "greyscale"),
  colorblind = FALSE,
  medium = "toy",
  background = NULL,
  min_contrast = 3
)

Arguments

palettes

Character vector of one or more palette names; see tf_palette_names(). Team names are not accepted; use tf_palette_names(team = ...) to expand a team.

n

Number of colours wanted.

style

One of "light" (white background), "dark" (near-black background) or "greyscale" (white background, judged by lightness alone).

colorblind

Logical. Require the colours to stay distinct under simulated deuteranopia, protanopia and tritanopia?

medium

Medium for plain palette names; see tf_media().

background

Optional background colour overriding the one implied by style, as a hex string.

min_contrast

Minimum WCAG 2 contrast ratio a colour must have against the background to be considered. Set to 1 to disable the filter.

Value

A character vector of n hex colours with class "tf_palette", named by the palette each colour came from, and with attributes min_distance (smallest pairwise distance under the chosen criterion), style, colorblind and background.

Details

The selection runs in three steps.

  1. Pool. The colours of every palette in palettes are combined, with duplicates removed. Names may be plain ("optimus_prime") or carry a medium suffix ("optimus_prime_cartoon"); plain names use medium.

  2. Filter for the background. Colours whose WCAG 2 contrast ratio against the background is below min_contrast are dropped, so a light-mode selection never contains a near-white and a dark-mode selection never contains a near-black. The background is white for "light" and "greyscale" and near-black ("#121212") for "dark" unless background is given. The default of 3 is the WCAG minimum for graphical objects; lower it to keep more colours, raise it for text.

  3. Choose. Every pair of remaining colours is scored by its distance in CIE Lab (CIE76). With colorblind = TRUE the distance is the smallest of the normal-vision distance and the distances after simulating deuteranopia, protanopia and tritanopia (Machado, Oliveira and Fernandes 2009), so two colours only count as distinct if every viewer can tell them apart. With style = "greyscale" only the lightness difference counts, so the colours survive conversion to grey. The n colours whose closest pair is farthest apart are chosen (a maximum-dispersion subset, found exhaustively when the pool is small and by greedy seeding plus swap search otherwise), then ordered so that each colour is as different as possible from those before it.

The result is a categorical palette: it does not try to build a gradient. The smallest pairwise distance in the selection is returned as the min_distance attribute; values above about 20 are comfortably distinct, and below about 12 two colours will be hard to tell apart. If the pool cannot supply n colours after filtering, the function errors and says how many it had, so add palettes or lower min_contrast.

See also

tf_find_palettes() to shortlist whole palettes instead; tf_palette_stats() for the underlying measures.

Examples

# five colours for a white-background plot, from the two leaders
tf_pick(c("optimus_prime", "megatron"), n = 5)
#> Transformers pick of 5 colours from optimus_prime + megatron
#> light background #FFFFFF, min distance 21.7
#> optimus_prime = #D0202A
#> optimus_prime = #1F3E8F
#> megatron = #8C9095
#> megatron = #2A2A2A
#> megatron = #6B3FA0


# the same for a dark theme, and colour-blind safe
tf_pick(c("optimus_prime", "megatron"), n = 4, style = "dark", colorblind = TRUE)
#> Transformers pick of 4 colours from optimus_prime + megatron
#> dark background #121212, colorblind-safe, min distance 22
#> optimus_prime = #D0202A
#> megatron = #C9CBCF
#> optimus_prime = #F2D23C
#> megatron = #8C9095


# a whole team, cartoon colours, printable in greyscale
tf_pick(tf_palette_names(team = "Combaticons"), n = 4,
        style = "greyscale", medium = "cartoon")
#> Transformers pick of 4 colours from onslaught_cartoon + brawl_cartoon + swindle_cartoon + blast_off_cartoon + vortex_cartoon + bruticus_cartoon
#> greyscale background #FFFFFF, min distance 4.5
#> onslaught_cartoon = #2B2B2B
#> onslaught_cartoon = #4E6E3E
#> swindle_cartoon = #5A3E8A
#> onslaught_cartoon = #2E5A8A


library(ggplot2)
cols <- tf_pick(tf_palette_names(team = "Predacons"), n = 3, colorblind = TRUE)
ggplot(mpg, aes(displ, hwy, colour = drv)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = unname(cols)) +
  theme_minimal()
